reason: The cited evidence shows tungsten improves high-temperature wear resistance in a different HEA system (AlCoCrFeNi) at 800 °C, but provides no data on room-temperature behavior, tribolayer formation, or the specific CoCrFeNi matrix. The key premises about adaptive tribolayer formation, lattice distortion effects, and low-temperature mechanisms are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Tungsten doping promotes formation of a stable, adaptive lubricious tribolayer in CoCrFeNi
Tungsten addition increases lattice distortion and promotes surface segregation under sliding
At lower temperatures, tungsten accelerates microstructural refinement and lowers shear strength
At higher temperatures, tungsten facilitates a protective lubricious phase that minimizes wear
The intervention yields lower friction and wear than undoped CoCrFeNi from RT to 800 °C
